newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli dollar bonds end lower amid uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Israeli dollar bonds end lower amid uncertainty.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed lower on Tuesday as traders sold off dollar-linked bonds in early trading on speculation that the shekel would appreciate, traders said.
Indices:
* Government bonds general: -0.1 pct to 107.11
* CPI-linked government bonds: -0.16 pct to 106.93
* Unlinked government bonds: +0.16 pct to 108.51
* Dollar-linked government bonds: -0.24 pct to 105.46
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.05 pct to 106.68
Volume including Makams was 196 million shekels.
"The whole market moved on the story that they were going to open the (foreign currency trading) band and cut interest rates to balance things out," said Ron Weisberg of IBI Investment House.

Early Tuesday morning Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced that he had agreed at an all-night meeting with Finance Minister Dan Meridor and Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel to a package of budget cuts and foreign currency liberalisations.

But the three failed to reach an agreement on widening the shekel's trading band against the basket of foreign currencies to which it is pegged, fuelling uncertainly in the forex market on Tuesday. Netanyahu has called a special cabinet meeting for later on Tuesday to present a compromise.
An expanded trading band is widely expected to lead to an appreciation of the shekel.

"The stock exchange this morning raised the three percent restriction on movement on bonds to six percent to allow traders more freedom," Weisberg said. "This created some panic in the market, with dollar-linked bonds being hit hard in early trading."
"In the end it wasn't a slaughter and dollar-linked bonds didn't do too badly," he said.
Trading in dollar-linked bonds was a heavy 47.5 million shekels, he added.

"Because the shekel closed almost unchanged against the dollar at the end of the trading day there was demand for dollar-linked bonds out of the stock market," said Gila Shkury of Israel Discount Bank.
The shekel representative rate was fixed almost unchanged against the dollar and basket of foreign currencies on Tuesday after the Bank of Israel intervened on a massive scale, forex dealers said.

Weisberg said there was strong demand for unlinked bonds and Makams on Tuesday because of the low May consumer price index and because traders are expecting a cut in interest rates as part of the economic package being hammered out by Netanyahu.
The May CPI rose 0.5 percent, well under analysts' expectations of 0.7 to 0.9 percent.
The Bank of Israel will announce its July monetary programme including interest rates on June 23. The base rate has been unchanged at 13.9 percent since the end of February.
"Short-term CPI-linked bonds are still under pressure because of the low CPI," Weisberg said, adding that prices of CPI-linked long bonds were stable.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
($1 = 3.42 shekels)
